entry.summary: In the previous article, we introduced the HTTP OPTIONS method and learned that it is commonly used to discover the capabilities of a resource. Now it's time to understand why browsers sometimes send an OPTIONS request before the actual request. This process is called a Preflight Request. Isn't CORS Enough? As we've already learned, CORS is a browser security mechanism. If the server does not allow the requesting Origin, the browser prevents JavaScript from accessing the response. However, this raises an important question. What if the request itself could perform a sensitive operation on the server? For example, imagine a Cross-Origin request using the DELETE or PUT method. HTTP QUERY is here: what changes for frontend data fetching?
entry.summary: You’ve probably hit this frustrating moment: your frontend needs to fetch data with complex filters or queries, but GET just won’t cut it because your URL grows unwieldy or exceeds length limits. So you switch to POST, shove your JSON search parameters in the body, and call it a day. Except now your POST request is meant to be a safe, read-only fetch. But HTTP semantics say POST is neither safe nor idempotent. That kills caching on CDNs, disables certain browser optimizations, and confuses intermediaries. You’re stuck in a weird limbo. Enter HTTP QUERY , the new kid on the block, standardized by RFC 10008 in June 2026. It's safe and idempotent like GET but also lets you send a request body like POST. entry.title: Reject Agent Tasks Before Queue Age Breaks the SLO
entry.summary:
A queue can accept work long after it has lost the ability to finish that work on time. “Message accepted” is not availability when the task's deadline will expire before a worker starts it. Apply backpressure at admission using predicted queue age. For one worker pool: predicted_wait_seconds = queued_work_seconds / effective_worker_concurrency
Use observed service time by task class rather than one global average. A five-second lint task and a twenty-minute repository migration should not contribute the same queue weight. Admit a request only when: predicted_wait + p95_service_time + safety_margin < task_deadline
